_comment: Labor-market figures shown on the employers page (BRIEF §7: cite LA/OC COE, BLS OEWS, CA EDD, Lightcast; APA 7; never invent statistics). Every figure names its source id below, and every source lists the page the figure was read from. Primary sites could not be opened from the build sandbox on 2026-09-06, so each number was confirmed from at least two independent search results quoting the primary page; TODO(vincent): spot-check each figure against its URL before relying on it, then update `checked`.

adoption.label: Adoption
adoption.title: Employers have adopted AI. Skills are the bottleneck.
adoption.takeaway: In two years, regular use of AI in at least one business function went from just over half of organizations to nearly nine in ten. The same surveys say the missing piece is people who can use it well.

trend.title: Organizations using AI in at least one business function
trend.subtitle: Share of respondents to McKinsey's global surveys, by survey wave.

meters.title: What employers say about AI skills

items.label: of leaders would not hire someone without AI skills
would rather hire a less experienced candidate who has AI skills
items.detail: Than a more experienced one who does not.

items.label: of employers name skills gaps as the main barrier to transforming their business
of employers in manufacturing and finance name a lack of skills as the main barrier to adopting AI
items.detail: Over half report a growing need for highly skilled workers.

pay.label: Pay
pay.title: AI skills carry a pay premium, in tech roles and outside them.
pay.takeaway: Postings that ask for AI skills advertise more pay than the same jobs without them, and the occupations that use the program's skills earn well above the all-occupation median.

wages.title: Median annual wage, May 2025
wages.subtitle: U.S. occupations that use the skills this program teaches, against all occupations.

meters.title: Advertised pay premium for AI skills

items.label: higher advertised pay in U.S. postings that ask for AI skills
items.detail: About $18,000 a year more, from 1.3 billion postings.

items.label: higher with two or more AI skills in the same posting
average wage premium for AI skills across a billion job ads on six continents

growth.label: Growth
growth.title: The occupations that use these skills are projected to grow fastest.
growth.takeaway: BLS expects AI to add demand for building models, analyzing data and integrating applications into business practice, and to reduce demand in some arts and design, sales and administrative roles.

bars.title: Projected U.S. employment growth, 2025 to 2035
bars.subtitle: Percent change in employment. Hover or focus a bar for the May 2025 median wage where published.

growth.note: Computer and mathematical occupations are projected to grow 10.1% over 2024–34, more than three times the all-occupation rate.

demand.label: Demand
demand.title: Demand for AI skills has spread well beyond tech jobs.
demand.takeaway: Half of the postings that ask for AI skills are now outside IT and computer science, and California posts more of them than any other state.

countries.title: Share of job postings that mention AI skills, 2025
countries.subtitle: Percent of all postings in each labor market. The United States is highlighted.

states.title: AI job postings by state, 2025
states.subtitle: The three states with the most postings. California's share is about 17% of the U.S. total.

items.label: of postings that ask for AI skills are outside IT and computer science
items.detail: Postings mentioning generative AI skills in non-tech roles grew about 800% from 2022 to 2024.

local.label: Local
local.title: Los Angeles and Orange County are already a major AI labor market.
local.takeaway: The region ranks fourth in North America for AI specialists, computer and mathematical work pays well above the metro average, and the county expects 1.6 million openings this decade.

hourly.title: Mean hourly wage, May 2025
hourly.subtitle: Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim against the national average.
hourly.highlight: Computer and mathematical occupations, LA metro

rows.name: Computer and mathematical occupations, LA metro

openings.title: Job openings projected in Los Angeles County, 2022 to 2032
openings.subtitle: New jobs from growth against openings from people leaving occupations. Professional and business services adds 81,200 jobs over the period.

tiles.label: largest AI-specialist workforce in North America
tiles.detail: 13,605 AI specialists in Los Angeles and Orange County, behind only San Francisco, Seattle and New York.

tiles.label: healthcare jobs Orange County expects to add by 2035
tiles.detail: The county's largest growth sector; aerospace and defense, the clean economy, life sciences and high tech add about 8,000 more.

local.note: The Los Angeles and Orange County Centers of Excellence publish the regional labor-market research California's community colleges use for program planning.

world.label: World
world.title: Worldwide, AI is expected to transform far more jobs than it removes.
world.takeaway: Employers surveyed by the World Economic Forum expect a net gain of 78 million jobs by 2030; the ILO finds one job in four has some exposure to generative AI, most of it transformation rather than replacement.

jobs.title: Jobs created and displaced worldwide by 2030, as expected by employers
jobs.subtitle: Millions of jobs. Survey of over 1,000 employers across 22 industries and 55 economies.

exposure.title: Share of jobs with some exposure to generative AI
exposure.subtitle: Percent of employment, by country income group. Clerical work is the most exposed.

items.label: of workers' existing skills are expected to change by 2030
items.detail: AI and big data is the fastest-growing skill.

items.label: growth in jobs that require AI skills, against 9% for all jobs
items.detail: Across a billion job ads on six continents.

latest.label: Latest U.S. jobs report, August 2026
latest.text: Payrolls rose by 162,000 and unemployment held at 4.1%. The information industry lost jobs. A monthly reading, revised twice; it is context, not a trend.
